### P2-02 — make the throttle's scope/phase explicit

- Location: A `REPORT.md` line 46, “every 256 such calls.”
- [ClientContext implementation lines 1100–1110](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/client_context.cpp#L1100-L1110) uses a function-local `thread_local` counter. Short-circuit evaluation increments it only when the deadline is valid and the earlier user-interrupt check did not throw. This definition does not reset it at query start; it is not a query-global or per-query-reset quantum.
- Hand counterexample to an over-reading: if a thread's counter already has residue 255, the next eligible call checks the deadline; residue 0 gives 256 eligible calls. This is a source/math illustration, not an observed counter or timing result.
- Required additive qualification: state thread-local, phase-persistent, deadline-valid eligible calls; do not infer a new-query first-poll count or wall-time guarantee. A already rejects the wall-time inference, so this does not overturn its main conclusion.

## Substantive source findings

1. **Request versus completion is correctly separated.** The exact connection specification supports same-connection cross-thread interruption; the implementation records a cancel generation and requests interruption. Result classification needs both an interrupt exception and generation change. Step's sticky cancellation status differs from fetch/drain's interrupt error. The report does not invent causal uniqueness under races or infer stopped callbacks/cleanup from request return.
2. **Callback and host safe points are not conflated.** The actual context definition is scope-bound with an already-held context/transaction. Scalar and table callbacks are called synchronously and their slot checked after return. The table bridge can repeatedly claim empty batches in its own loop without an explicit check there. A bounded individual callback does not prove a bounded bridge interval. Step's synchronous task call does not substantiate hard preemption or a maximum duration, notwithstanding the optimistic bounded/nonblocking specification wording.
3. **The bounded negative capability wording is appropriate.** A reports no direct local poll found in its named inspected specifications; it explicitly excludes generated headers, other modules and all planner paths from an absence proof. This peer checked the actual context definition and relevant bridge/factory text, not every API module. It does not independently certify global absence or reopen any unavailable request.
4. **Deadline/admission claims remain appropriately conditional.** Deadline setup follows some query/transaction setup, uses checked addition, and may leave the deadline disabled on unrepresentable addition. Task entry deliberately checks user interruption without the deadline there. Existing input chunks/argument Values precede application callbacks. Local reservations cannot retroactively admit upstream SQL LIST construction, folding or materialization. A identifies that prerequisite rather than claiming it is solved.
5. **Error/health distinctions are supported.** Return codes, optional stale/absent detail, stack-borrowed callback slots and fallibility defaults have actual source support. Both null setters reject null in implementation despite YAML no-op promises. Text assignment has no local wrapper, so a universal helper-safety claim would be unjustified; A makes no such claim or selected repair. Generic FATAL classification must not hide the additional INTERNAL invalidation branches in actual query failure/cleanup. These are conditional paths, not proof that every internal failure takes the same cleanup route. Result destruction adopts/nulls the handle before fallible finalization; SQL abort is not rollback of arbitrary external store state.
6. **Ownership and accounting claims are useful, bounded facts.** Fetched chunks are owned; their vectors/views and collection scan data have different expiry rules. A live chunk handle alone cannot extend a worker scan buffer's lifetime. Deep copies construct storage; collection clear retains buffers whereas reset releases row storage according to the selected spec. View extraction may flatten a dictionary child; reference aliases, and per-cell Value extraction allocates an owned object. These facts justify coexistence/capacity/alias charges, not an exact allocator/RSS/capacity oracle. Factory/database accounting does not establish coverage of private dictionaries/indexes/bindings/strings.
7. **The mathematical latency expression is conditional, not measured.** With at most q units until a check, cost at most c per unit and total other uninterruptible work at most L over that interval, q·c+L bounds that interval's modeled work/cost. Detection/check/cleanup, scheduling and token delivery need their own premises for a latency statement. No finite row/chunk count alone supplies those premises. The ancillary execution-model paper is architectural context, not a performance forecast; this peer did not re-audit its empirical study.
